category_title: Middle school student with autism and language impairment exhibiting property destruction and self-injury when frustrated
minimal_context: Carrie is working on a three-step measurement task during a math class in a general education setting.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Carrie, it is time for math. First, take your ruler, then measure the length of this poster, and finally write the number down on your paper.

STUDENT: (Looks confused and stares at the ruler without picking it up)

TUTOR: How are you going to start?

STUDENT: (Makes an unintelligible sound and begins engaging in self-stimulation by rocking back and forth in her chair)

TUTOR: Just go ahead and do the three steps I told you to do.

STUDENT: (Grabs the poster off the desk, tears it up, and begins hitting her own arm)

options.A: Ask the student what they think went wrong with the measurement task instead of telling them what went wrong.
options.B: Provide access to general education classmates, allowing the student to observe and model their peers' behaviors during the math class.
options.C: Use interview prompts and the Academic Volitional Strategy Inventory to measure the student's perception of self-regulated learning during the math class.
options.D: Radically remove time constraints for the measurement task, slowing down the pace as much as required by the student.
